mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where CPI YoY > 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a single month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE increases > 0.5% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 2% month-over-month signals weakening consumer demand, which negatively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where RSAFS decreases > 2% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals strengthening economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances where INDPRO increases > 1% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a loosening of monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS decreases.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases by more than 200,000 jobs in a month, it signals a tight labor market and strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 MoM.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% month-over-month and retail sales (RSAFS) increase by more than 1% month-over-month, it signals strong consumer demand and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 5% MoM and RSAFS increases > 1% MoM
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances where HOUST increases > 5% MoM and RSAFS increases > 1% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: During a period of economic expansion, a decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a potential supply chain disruption, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO decreases > 1% MoM during economic expansion.
